svg.text: wicket: what runs where, and where the trust boundaries are
Green: trusted, holds secrets and keys. Blue: a node, no long-lived secrets. Red dashed: a box, untrusted, no network, no secrets. Arrows: who talks to whom.
Runs as the wicket system user. Issues authority, takes human approvals, keeps the record.
Operators' CLI over a unix socket.
policy grants read / run / revoke per group.
Approving, update and keys: root or a passkey.
Runs, approvals, activity, start a run.
Passkeys only; every approval is a signed
WebAuthn action. HTTPS with ACME, or
Start the run's box on a node, stream its events, enforce its budget and timeout.
Hold what must stay central: credential injection and swaps for forwarded hosts,
the model credential and budget (the node's model proxy relays here), the MCP
gateway's ledger-backed tools, and the relay for links between boxes on any nodes.
Survive a restart: a new build re-attaches to running runs (#151).
Feed signer: each box's Biscuit token,
Makes reality match the ledger: ends lost
runs, stops orphaned boxes, adopts boxes
the hosts it may go to.
Streams the ledger, hibernation bundles and audit to an S3-compatible store; tested restore.
The control host's built-in node and every enrolled Linux host run the same runtime, wicket node serve, reached over a
control channel (unix socket, or ssh with a pinned host key) that carries the signed feed: the green arrow.
Starts and owns its boxes; they outlive a serve restart and are adopted again.
Egress proxy per box: decides each request at the edge, from the box's Biscuit token and the node's
verified replica of the signed feed. No call to the control host per request.
Inspected hosts: TLS terminated with the node's name-constrained CA, every request decided and audited.
Spliced hosts (allowed wholesale, no credential): decided on the hostname, encrypted bytes relayed.
Wicket DNS and the HTTP/3 (QUIC) relay. Model proxy and MCP gateway for each box (relaying to the run).
Keeps its own hash-chained audit log and ships it. If the control host is unreachable, keeps deciding
from its feed while it is fresh, then reads only, then refuses (#152/#153: until grants expire).
A box: one per run (gVisor; untrusted)
runsc · --network none · no capabilities · read-only root · resource limits · no secrets inside
Or a pinned program without an agent.
Workspace: a copy, or a folder in place;
DNS and UDP for HTTP/3; the box's stdin
Relays each to a unix socket bind-mounted in.
What a box can do, and what decides it
Reach: only hosts, methods and paths its zone allows; anything else becomes a request a human approves
or denies, as a grant with a lifetime. Forbid rules always win, even over a grant.
Model: only the model endpoints, within its budget; the real credential is added outside the box.
Children: spawn narrower boxes (their tokens attenuate the parent's); wider ones need a human.
Links: talk to another box, on any node, only where both zones allow it.
Hibernate and wake: its whole filesystem and session, on any node.
Nothing in the box can reach the host's Docker, the node's keys or another box's sockets.
Browser: the console, with a passkey.
Audit sinks and the state store
JSON lines, OTLP, an object store;
Credential added by the run (central) or,
later, by a lease on the node (#152).
Hosts in a zone's reach, through the node's
egress proxy only. Private and metadata
1. The agent's HTTPS request goes to wicket.internal:3128, through wicket-fwd, to its node's egress proxy over a unix socket.
2. The node canonicalizes it (or refuses), classifies its risk, and checks it against the box's token: block 0 from the zone's policy
(Cedar compiled into Biscuit at issuance: #51), plus grant blocks a human approved, each with a lifetime. Forbids always win.
3. Allowed: inspected or spliced to the host. Not allowed: a pending request in the console; the agent waits with await_grant.
4. Every decision is in the node's audit log, shipped to the control host's hash-chained ledger and on to any sinks.
Planned items are marked with their issue numbers. Source: docs/explanation/design.md; this diagram replaces docs/poc-architecture.svg.
